input.final_result:
Answer: Amazon (AMZN) plans to spend the most on capex in 2025, as of April 7, 2025.

Guidance as of that date:
- Amazon (AMZN): About $100 billion. <cite index="3-1">Amazon said Thursday it plans to boost its capital expenditures to $100 billion in 2025, as it continues its investments in artificial intelligence.</cite> Amazon's CEO also said <cite index="3-10">"We spent $26.3 billion in capex in Q4, and I think that is reasonably representative of what you expect an annualized capex rate in 2025."</cite> Annualizing that quarter gives about $105.2 billion, so the run-rate implies even more than the $100 billion figure. Amazon's total also <cite index="4-11">includes the buildout of its e-commerce fulfillment network and retail stores, which means it's not directly comparable to Microsoft, Google and others.</cite>
- Alphabet (GOOG): <cite index="17-9">"We are confident about the opportunities ahead, and to accelerate our progress, we expect to invest approximately $75 billion in capital expenditures in 2025," Pichai said</cite>.
- Meta (META): <cite index="11-8">We anticipate our full year 2025 capital expenditures will be in the range of $60-65 billion.</cite> The midpoint is $62.5 billion.

Comparison:
- Amazon's ~$100 billion vs. Alphabet's ~$75 billion is about 33.33% more.
- Amazon's ~$100 billion vs. Meta's $62.5 billion midpoint is about 60.00% more.
- Alphabet is second and Meta is third.

Note: Some search results were dated after April 7, 2025 (for example, later raises to Meta's 2025 capex range). I excluded them because they were not available as of the stated date.
